# Volume models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

11 volume models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: a CT volume `[D, H, W]` in Hounsfield units and its voxel spacing in mm (`volume.read_nifti` reads both from a NIfTI file). Output: a class index per voxel `[D, H, W]` on the input grid (0 = background). Encoder models (nnFoundation) take a CT or MRI volume and give its encoder feature maps. For a trained nnU-Net v2 folder or checkpoint, see the [nnU-Net v2 loader](../api/volume.md#nnu-net-v2).

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.10.0+cu130, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 200x200: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured; no kernels = the family has no kernels backend (reason under its table). Reserved memory is the allocator's cache: kernels (CUDA graphs, cuDNN workspaces) can reserve a few percent to some tens of percent more than portable at the same allocated peak.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB (MLX)](../devices/apple-m1-pro-mlx-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## nnFoundation

nnFoundation (DKFZ): self-supervised 3D encoders (a convolutional one and a vision transformer) pre-trained on 2.1 million CT, MRI and PET volumes; they turn a volume into feature maps for your own medical models. Share-alike weights (CC-BY-SA-4.0): fine-tuned models keep the licence.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nnfoundation-cnn` | synthetic (200x200) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 501<br>274<br>248<br>232<br>170<br>255 (encoder on a normalized, padded volume only; memory estimated) | 7247 / 8734<br>3818 / 4628<br>2368 / 3330<br>2325 / 3330<br>5067 / 5110<br>3374 / 3398 |
| `nnfoundation-vit` | synthetic (192x192) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp32 | OOM<br>1930<br>1816<br>1699<br>1440<br>7024 (standalone encoder, fixed 192³, TF32 disabled) | –<br>3930 / 4298<br>1510 / 1564<br>1510 / 1564<br>1406 / 1484<br>8452 / 8452 |

### Measured

A small subset of real CT cases of the TotalSegmentator dataset (not the full test split), each run at its card's spacing (1.5 or 3 mm) in the same pipeline; mean over the cases of the Dice (0 to 1) averaged over the classes present, against the ground-truth segmentations (vertebrae_L6 of the subset has no counterpart and is skipped). Original = TotalSegmentator 2.18.0, default fp16 autocast. Encoder models have no task head, so they are judged by their output: the encoder feature maps against the original fp32 maps (cosine similarity, worst case over the cases and the mean over the maps; relative L2 error, mean). Original (fp32) is the reference; the original fp16 row shows the error the original itself has in half precision. For the standalone ViT TensorRT comparison, both runs used the same normalized 192³ CT crops and FP32 with TF32 disabled. Relative L2 is the mean over the eight cases. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| `nnfoundation-vit` | TotalSegmentator test subset (8 CT cases), encoder features vs the original fp32: cosine (worst case) / relative L2 | 1.00000 / 0 | 0.99947 / 0.01672 | 0.99950 / 0.0165 | 1.00000 / 2.349e-05 | 0.99940 / 0.02129 |  |  |

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.8e-06 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.15 % and p99 <= 1.1 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `features`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nnfoundation-cnn` | 0.00063 / 0.00378 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `vol_norm@2f1c9c06c950:sm_120` |
| `nnfoundation-vit` | 0.0067 / 0.03039 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `vol_norm@2f1c9c06c950:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- CUDA portable and kernels accept stream=True to stage CNN levels or ViT blocks from pinned host memory. On the 192³ nnFoundation ViT reference, peak allocated memory during load and inference on an RTX 5060 Ti fell from 1,665 to 673 MiB in both modes.
- Kernels peak allocated is equal to portable, but the cuDNN workspace next to the large conv maps (1.4 GiB and 0.3 GiB workspaces) fragments the allocator: peak reserved is ~580 MiB above portable.
- A standalone fixed 192³ FP32 TensorRT ViT engine matched portable FP32 encoder features on eight CT crops. The standalone run took 7.02 s per crop with an estimated 8,452 MiB peak, versus 9.46 s and 2,864 MiB for portable FP32.

</details>

## nnInteractive

nnInteractive (DKFZ): a promptable 3D segmenter: click a point, draw a box or a scribble on any structure in a CT, MRI, PET or microscopy volume and it returns that structure's 3D mask; further prompts (positive or negative) refine it. Non-commercial weights (CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0).

Commercial use: **no** (weights: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0).

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nninteractive` | synthetic (200x200) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 705<br>460<br>209<br>193<br>162<br>fails: The TensorRT export accepts prepared 192³ network patches. | 7156 / 8408<br>4076 / 4636<br>2423 / 2772<br>2423 / 2772<br>3643 / 3832<br>– |

## TotalSegmentator

TotalSegmentator (University Hospital Basel): nnU-Net v2 networks that label 117 anatomical structures (organs, bones, muscles, vessels) in CT volumes, at 1.5 mm (five networks) or 3 mm (one, faster). Commercially usable (Apache-2.0 code and weights).

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `totalsegmentator-total` | synthetic (200x200) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 47779<br>45630<br>1977<br>1647<br>1595<br>1582 (five nnU-Net patch networks with eager volume processing) | 8150 / 8604<br>2640 / 2874<br>2017 / 2244<br>1219 / 1638<br>1697 / 1984<br>6646 / 7136 |
| `totalsegmentator-total-3mm` | synthetic (200x200) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 7304<br>7270<br>70.3<br>71.8<br>63.1<br>74.4 (patch network, standalone build) | 5358 / 5698<br>2010 / 2684<br>962 / 1050<br>913 / 1376<br>907 / 1030<br>2909 / 2970 |
